title: Nimble Reserve Buckets: modular reserved GPU bundles + enterprise security survey
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Objective: Define and pilot 'Nimble Reserve Buckets' — a modular reserved GPU offering that lets customers compose small, medium, and large commit buckets (measured in GPU-hours) with optional burst credits and transparent SLA tiers. We will pair this pricing experiment with an enterprise security questionnaire template and contract clauses for burst/fallback behavior.

Background: Customers (esp. mid-market and AI-native startups) ask for more granular reserved offerings: smaller minimum commitments, predictable baseline throughput, and a clear path to burst. Current offerings are heavy-weight (large monthly commits) which creates friction for teams that need predictable costs but not full rack reservations. Sales and Legal also ask for a standardized security questionnaire to accelerate procurement for Dedicated and Private customers.

Scope:
- Define three modular bucket sizes (nano, standard, pro) with per-GPU-hour commit pricing and explicit burst credit pricing and exhaustion behavior.
- Define SLA tiers tied to reserved baseline throughput and burst availability: Standard (SLA on baseline), Premium (SLA on baseline + guaranteed burst fallback), and Economy (best-effort autoscale).
- Create initial contract language describing burst credit accounting, preemption policy for burst when region contention occurs, and guaranteed fallback model.
- Produce a security questionnaire draft focused on Dedicated/Private deployments: KMS, HSM, encryption, SSO, RBAC, network isolation, audit logs, pen-test evidence, DSGVO/SOC2 references, and on-prem upgrade/patch windows.
- Build a pricing simulator spreadsheet and one-pager for sales.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Pricing granularity improves PLG motion but increases ops complexity for capacity planning.
- Guaranteeing burst is costly; we propose a hybrid: small guaranteed burst for Premium and larger soft burst credits subject to preemption/priority policy.
- Contract simplicity vs. legal risk: initial pilot will use standardized addendum that limits liability for burst preemption during force majeure or capacity exhaustion.

Success metrics:
- Conversion rate from trial to paid for customers < $10k/month committed: target +12% vs baseline.
- Average time-to-contract for Dedicated under $250k ARR: reduce from 38 days to < 14 days.
- Attach rate to Premium SLA among bucket buyers: 25% within 90 days.
- Measured delta in cost per effective GPU-hour (including burst): < 15% variance vs committed baseline for 95% of customers.

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix (nano/standard/pro) with per-GPU-hour and monthly commit options.
- Burst credit mechanics doc + exhaustion/fallback playbook.
- Draft security questionnaire (for sales/legal).
- Pricing simulator and sales one-pager.
- Pilot cohort runbook and success dashboard queries.

Stakeholders: PM (owner), Sales ENG (solutions), Legal (contract wording), Security/Compliance (questionnaire sign-off), Infra (capacity modeling), Console (billing display).

Risks:
- Underpricing burst could cause capacity exhaustion; mitigations: simulate worst-case, introduce soft caps and surge premiums.
- Security questions may reveal gaps for on-prem; mitigation: map to Private product SKUs and raise an escalation path to R&D for required features.

Timeline / next milestones:
- 2026-03-05: final pricing matrix and SLA tiers (done, internal review).
- 2026-03-12: security questionnaire first draft submitted to Security (status: review).
- 2026-03-20: pilot cohort selection + sales enablement materials (target).
- 2026-04-01: pilot launch; begin measuring adoption and contract velocity.
